NASB.1: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, 'Do not fear, Abram, I am a shield to you; Your reward shall be very great.'
NASB.2: Abram said, 'O Lord GOD, what will You give me, since I am childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?'
NASB.3: And Abram said, 'Since You have given no offspring to me, one born in my house is my heir.'
NASB.4: Then behold, the word of the LORD came to him, saying, 'This man will not be your heir; but one who will come forth from your own body, he shall be your heir.'
NASB.5: And He took him outside and said, 'Now look toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.' And He said to him, 'So shall your descendants be.'
NASB.6: Then he believed in the LORD; and He reckoned it to him as righteousness.
NASB.7: And He said to him, 'I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to possess it.'
NASB.8: He said, 'O Lord GOD, how may I know that I will possess it?'
NASB.9: So He said to him, 'Bring Me a three year old heifer, and a three year old female goat, and a three year old ram, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.'
NASB.10: Then he brought all these to Him and cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but he did not cut the birds.
NASB.11: The birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
NASB.12: Now when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, terror [and] great darkness fell upon him.
NASB.13: [God] said to Abram, 'Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, where they will be enslaved and oppressed four hundred years.
NASB.14: 'But I will also judge the nation whom they will serve, and afterward they will come out with many possessions.
NASB.15: 'As for you, you shall go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.
NASB.16: 'Then in the fourth generation they will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet complete.'
NASB.17: It came about when the sun had set, that it was very dark, and behold, [there appeared] a smoking oven and a flaming torch which passed between these pieces.
NASB.18: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, 'To your descendants I have given this land, From the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates:
NASB.19: the Kenite and the Kenizzite and the Kadmonite
NASB.20: and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Rephaim
NASB.21: and the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Girgashite and the Jebusite.'

NLT.1: Some time later, the LORD spoke to Abram in a vision and said to him, “Do not be afraid, Abram, for I will protect you, and your reward will be great.”
NLT.2: But Abram replied, “O Sovereign LORD, what good are all your blessings when I don’t even have a son? Since you’ve given me no children, Eliezer of Damascus, a servant in my household, will inherit all my wealth.
NLT.3: You have given me no descendants of my own, so one of my servants will be my heir.”
NLT.4: Then the LORD said to him, “No, your servant will not be your heir, for you will have a son of your own who will be your heir.”
NLT.5: Then the LORD took Abram outside and said to him, “Look up into the sky and count the stars if you can. That’s how many descendants you will have!”
NLT.6: And Abram believed the LORD, and the LORD counted him as righteous because of his faith.
NLT.7: Then the LORD told him, “I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land as your possession.”
NLT.8: But Abram replied, “O Sovereign LORD, how can I be sure that I will actually possess it?”
NLT.9: The LORD told him, “Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
NLT.10: So Abram presented all these to him and killed them. Then he cut each animal down the middle and laid the halves side by side; he did not, however, cut the birds in half.
NLT.11: Some vultures swooped down to eat the carcasses, but Abram chased them away.
NLT.12: As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a terrifying darkness came down over him.
NLT.13: Then the LORD said to Abram, “You can be sure that your descendants will be strangers in a foreign land, where they will be oppressed as slaves for 400 years.
NLT.14: But I will punish the nation that enslaves them, and in the end they will come away with great wealth.
NLT.15: (As for you, you will die in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.)
NLT.16: After four generations your descendants will return here to this land, for the sins of the Amorites do not yet warrant their destruction.”
NLT.17: After the sun went down and darkness fell, Abram saw a smoking firepot and a flaming torch pass between the halves of the carcasses.
NLT.18: So the LORD made a covenant with Abram that day and said, “I have given this land to your descendants, all the way from the border of Egypt to the great Euphrates River —
NLT.19: the land now occupied by the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,

NIV.1:
God’s Covenant With Abram
After this, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision:
“Do not be afraid, Abram.
I am your shield,
your very great reward.”
NIV.2: But Abram said, “O Sovereign Lord, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”
NIV.3: And Abram said, “You have given me no children; so a servant in my household will be my heir.”
NIV.4: Then the word of the Lord came to him: “This man will not be your heir, but a son coming from your own body will be your heir.”
NIV.5: He took him outside and said, “Look up at the heavens and count the stars—if indeed you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
NIV.6: Abram believed the Lord, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
NIV.7: He also said to him, “I am the Lord, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to take possession of it.”
NIV.8: But Abram said, “O Sovereign Lord, how can I know that I will gain possession of it?”
NIV.9: So the Lord said to him, “Bring me a heifer, a goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon.”
NIV.10: Abram brought all these to him, cut them in two and arranged the halves opposite each other; the birds, however, he did not cut in half.
NIV.11: Then birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
NIV.12: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him.
NIV.13: Then the Lord said to him, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
NIV.14: But I will punish the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.
NIV.15: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age.
NIV.16: In the fourth generation your descendants will come back here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure.”
NIV.17: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces.
NIV.18: On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram and said, “To your descendants I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates—
NIV.19: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
